description: Create the self-contained CRAN-checkable R sub-package `bucketimpute` implementing Bucketed Imputation Regression (BIR) exactly per bucketed-imputation-regression-spec.md, with the ONE mandated deviation: use the `lars` package (NOT glmnet) for the CV-selected lasso. Package lives at /projects/sandbox/earth/bucketimpute/ and exports fit_bir(), predict.bir() and the S3 class 'bir', plus print.bir/summary.bir (plot.bir optional). Independent of the earth C sources; no earth rebuild.
steps: Create package skeleton at /projects/sandbox/earth/bucketimpute/: DESCRIPTION (Package: bucketimpute; Title/Description explaining BIR; Version 0.1.0; Imports: earth, lars, stats; License: GPL-3 or same as a permissive choice; Encoding UTF-8; RoxygenNote), NAMESPACE (generated by roxygen), R/, man/, tests/. Add Authors@R placeholder.

Implement R/fit_bir.R: fit_bir(x, y, n = 10, min_bucket_rows = NULL, scale_floor = 1e-8, ...). (a) Coerce x to numeric matrix preserving/asserting column names (if NULL assign V1..Vp); assert all numeric, no NA, y numeric continuous. (b) Compute n+1 quantile cut-points of y with quantile(y, probs=seq(0,1,length.out=n+1), type=7). REQUIRE n>=2 (error otherwise). If the cut-points do not yield n DISTINCT non-empty buckets (heavy ties / near-binary y), stop() with a clear message naming the distinct-buckets problem (do NOT silently merge). (c) Assign rows to buckets 1..n via findInterval with all.inside/rightmost handling so every row lands in exactly one of n buckets. (d) Determine min_bucket_rows default: a documented sensible default (e.g. max(p+2, 10) or similar) ensuring each bucket has enough rows relative to p for degree-1 earth fits; if any bucket has fewer rows than min_bucket_rows, warn; if a bucket is truly too thin to fit (e.g. < 2 rows or < needed for earth), stop with clear message. (e) For each bucket k and each column j: fit earth(x_k[,-j, drop=FALSE], x_k[,j], degree=1, ...); record s_{k,j}=sqrt(mean(residuals^2)) FLOORED at scale_floor (document the floor); store the earth object. Preserve column names/order so model (k,j) predicts column j from the other p-1 columns. (f) Compute training affinities: N x n matrix where unusualness_{i,k}=sum_j |x_{i,j}-predict(earth_{k,j}, x_i[,-j])|/s_{k,j} and affinity=1/(1+unusualness). (g) CV-selected lasso via lars: fit lars(affinities, y, type='lasso'); run cv.lars(affinities, y, type='lasso', mode='fraction', plot.it=FALSE) and pick s_opt = index[which.min(cv)]; store lars fit, s_opt, mode='fraction'. (h) bucket_vars: var(y[bucket==k]) for each k (guard single-row buckets -> 0 or NA handled). (i) Return S3 'bir' object with fields: cuts, models, scales, lasso (lars fit), lasso_s, lasso_mode, bucket_vars, n, p, colnames, plus min_bucket_rows and scale_floor for transparency.

Implement R/predict_bir.R: predict.bir(object, newdata, type=c('response','affinity','all'), ...). Coerce newdata to matrix, reorder/select columns to object$colnames (error if any missing). Recompute unusualness+affinity per row using stored models and scales exactly as in training. Point prediction via predict(object$lasso, newx=affinities, s=object$lasso_s, mode=object$lasso_mode, type='fit')$fit. Predictive scale: normalize each row's affinities to sum 1 -> weights w_k; var_hat=sum(w_k*bucket_vars); se=sqrt(var_hat). Return: 'response' -> numeric vector of fits; 'affinity' -> the N x n affinity matrix; 'all' -> list/data.frame with fit, se, and affinities.

Implement R/methods_bir.R: print.bir (n buckets, p, chosen lars fraction s, class), summary.bir (as print plus e.g. range of residual scales, bucket_vars). plot.bir optional (may show affinity vs y or coefficient path) — keep simple or omit; if included it must not break R CMD check.

Write roxygen2 documentation on all exported functions making the ALGORITHM and the RETURNED OBJECT crystal-clear (the spec requires this). Explicitly document the lars-instead-of-glmnet substitution and the CV-min-MSE selection, the scale_floor, the min_bucket_rows rule, and the distinct-buckets error. Add a package-level doc (bucketimpute-package). Include a runnable @examples block using a tiny synthetic dataset (small n so examples run fast under R CMD check).

Add tests/ (tinytest preferred: tests/tinytest.R + inst/tinytest/test_bir.R, or plain scripts). Cover at minimum: (1) fit + predict round-trip on small synthetic data returns finite fits of correct length; type='affinity' returns N x n matrix; type='all' returns fit+se+affinities with se non-negative and correct length/shape. (2) fit_bir errors clearly on a near-binary y that cannot yield n distinct buckets. (3) se output shape/sign check. (4) n<2 errors.

Generate NAMESPACE and man/*.Rd with Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise("/projects/sandbox/earth/bucketimpute")'. Then build+install+check: cd /projects/sandbox/earth && R CMD build bucketimpute && R CMD INSTALL bucketimpute_0.1.0.tar.gz && R CMD check bucketimpute_0.1.0.tar.gz --no-manual. Fix any ERRORs; record WARNINGs/NOTEs. Remove the .tar.gz and .Rcheck artifacts before finishing (do not commit build artifacts).
acceptance_criteria: Directory /projects/sandbox/earth/bucketimpute is a self-contained R package with DESCRIPTION (Imports: earth, lars), NAMESPACE exporting fit_bir and predict.bir (S3 method), R/, and roxygen-generated man/*.Rd.
No use of glmnet anywhere; lasso is fit with lars and penalty selected by cv.lars at minimum CV MSE; predict.bir uses predict.lars with the stored s/mode.
R CMD check bucketimpute_0.1.0.tar.gz --no-manual completes with 0 ERRORs (WARNINGs/NOTEs documented).
Package tests pass, covering fit/predict round-trip, the distinct-buckets error, n<2 error, and se output shape.
The stored bir object contains cuts, models, scales, lasso, bucket_vars, n, p, colnames as required by the spec.
No build artifacts (tarball, .Rcheck) left in the working tree.
verification: cd /projects/sandbox/earth && Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise("bucketimpute")' && R CMD build bucketimpute && R CMD INSTALL bucketimpute_0.1.0.tar.gz && R CMD check bucketimpute_0.1.0.tar.gz --no-manual 2>&1 | tail -40
Confirm the check log shows 0 ERRORs and Status line; then remove bucketimpute_0.1.0.tar.gz and bucketimpute.Rcheck.
findings: Implemented self-contained package /projects/sandbox/earth/bucketimpute (Version 0.1.0; Imports earth, lars, stats; Suggests tinytest). Exports fit_bir(), predict.bir() S3 method, S3 class 'bir', plus print.bir and summary.bir (plot.bir omitted, allowed as optional). R CMD check bucketimpute_0.1.0.tar.gz --no-manual => Status: OK (0 ERRORs, 0 WARNINGs, 0 NOTEs). tinytest suite: 34 assertions, all OK. Mandated deviation implemented: no glmnet anywhere; lasso fit with lars::lars(type='lasso') and penalty selected via lars::cv.lars(type='lasso', mode='fraction', plot.it=FALSE) at s_opt = index[which.min(cv)] (lambda.min analogue); predict.bir uses predict.lars(newx=affinities, s=lasso_s, mode='fraction', type='fit')$fit. Edge cases: n>=2 enforced; distinct-buckets stop() (verified errors on near-binary y); min_bucket_rows default max(p+2,10) (warn if thin, hard error if <2 rows); residual scales floored at scale_floor (default 1e-8); column names/order preserved and reordered at predict time (verified shuffled-column predictions match). Stored bir object has cuts, models, scales (n x p matrix), lasso, lasso_s, lasso_mode, bucket_vars, n, p, colnames, min_bucket_rows, scale_floor. roxygen2 8.1.0 and tinytest were installed from p3m.dev during this feature. Build artifacts (tarball, .Rcheck) removed. Smoke test on synthetic data gave cor(fit,y)~0.79. No LaTeX -> checked with --no-manual.
